surface: Broker / local HTTP surface (routed auth broker)

nonContractChecks.reason: The same live management token fingerprint resolved /v1/auth/me with emailVerified=false before the durable Better Auth user row changed and with emailVerified=true after the durable row was updated to email_verified=true.

commands.observation: Created a disposable Better Auth user with emailVerified=false and received a browser session cookie on the routed broker host.
Started a live session handoff flow and received a flowId, deviceCode, authorizeUrl, and pollUrl.
Completed the bridged account flow with the authenticated browser session and received a 200 HTML response plus a hack_web_broker_session cookie.
Claimed the completed flow and received a managementToken whose claimed accountEmailVerified value remained false.
Before any durable-user update, the same management token resolved the disposable account with user.emailVerified=false.

commands.command: cd <repo>/services/auth-broker && TEST_EMAIL=<email> bun -e "import { neon } from "@neondatabase/serverless"; ... update "user" set email_verified = true ..."
commands.observation: Updated the durable Better Auth user row for the disposable account so email_verified became true after the management token had already been minted.
Using the same management token after the durable update, /v1/auth/me still authenticated the same user and now returned user.emailVerified=true.
The focused session-auth regression suite passed and corroborated the management-token hydration behavior in automation.

summary: Non-contract smoke passed. This milestone had no validation-contract assertions mapped through fulfills, so the routed broker management-token hydration follow-up was validated as a user-surface smoke instead.
